description:
Roman SX (Roman Space Exploration) is a solo-member team. Engineered single-handedly by a 14-year-old NASA's Cosmic Pathfinders participant utilizing industry-standard Python environments.

Roman SX builds an educational Space Mission Design Game about the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and a Sun–Earth L2 transfer. Players design a launch vehicle under budget, choose the best launch window possible, and fly an interactive ascent where throttle, staging, and communications decide success.
summary: A 2D rocket design and flight simulation game by Roman SX for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. This spaceflight simulator uses real-world physics and rocket science terms to help players understand terminology in aerospace industries. NASA Meteorite Landings Data is used as a dataset.
details:
Roman Space Program is a browser-based rocket-building and flight-simulation game I created for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026. Players assemble a launch vehicle using engines, fuel tanks, stages, boosters, and other components; choose a simulated launch window; and manage the rocket’s ascent toward a Sun–Earth L2 mission objective. During flight, players control throttle and staging while monitoring telemetry such as velocity, altitude, fuel, and thrust-to-weight ratio. The flight model is a simplified, physics-inspired 2D game simulation, not an 100% accurate orbital mechanics simulator. The site also includes a page featuring records from NASA’s Meteorite Landings dataset.

The project makes rocket design and launch operations interactive and approachable. Players explore how mass, thrust, fuel, staging, and launch conditions affect a mission. My intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space exploration and introduce aerospace concepts through hands-on play.

I considered how to make the controls and information understandable in a browser while still giving players meaningful vehicle-design and flight decisions. The project combines rocket assembly, launch planning, and live flight telemetry, while favoring an accessible game experience over scientific precision.

I built the project with Python and FastAPI, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Jinja2 templates, and JSON data. I used uv for Python dependency management and Render for hosting. The project runs in a web browser and requires no specialized hardware.

The project concept and Mission Design Sequence logic were my own. I used OpenAI’s ChatGPT, SpaceXSI’s Grok, Microsoft’s Copilot Fusion, and Google’s Gemini as coding assistance. My approximate estimates of SI contribution to the code are 5% for Python, 75% for HTML and CSS, and 55% for JavaScript. More information on SI's contribution can be accessed through https://roman-space-program.onrender.com/static/SI_USAGE.txt.


The usage of SI is genuinely to work efficiently given the time constraints. Super Intelligence is a multiplier to the project when its used in the right way. I hope its used in the best way.
